%% ============================================================
\section{Training Dynamics and Loss Decoupling}
\label{sec:training_dynamics}

The DeepSeek \texttt{exception\_only} results are consistent across all three seeds (99.33/99.50/99.33, $\sigma{=}$0.10pp), matching Qwen's cross-seed stability.
Epoch-level analysis shows mild degradation in seed 42: accuracy peaks at 99.83\% after epoch~1 but settles at 99.33\% by epoch~3 ($-$0.50pp), while seed 456 shows no degradation (99.33\% at both epochs).
Early stopping may yield marginal gains, but the epoch effect is small (${\leq}$0.5pp).
The practical recommendation: for deployment, use task-specific metrics (accuracy, fail recall) for checkpoint and seed selection rather than training loss, and train multiple seeds to select the best.

The contrast with VOTA is instructive: DeepSeek VOTA seed 42 accuracy monotonically increases from 78.15\% to 84.45\% across epochs, consistent with a performance limit from high trace truncation (91.7\% of samples; \S\ref{sec:tokenizer_analysis}).
Seeds 123/456, which avoid the truncation-sensitive initialization basin, achieve 99.16\%/99.33\%, indicating that the deficit is seed-specific rather than a fundamental model limitation.

%% ============================================================
\section{Deduplication Statistics}
\label{sec:dedup_stats}

Table~\ref{tab:dedup} reports the duplication rates across trace formats.
Because multiple passing solutions to the same problem produce identical (input, output) pairs in the \texttt{exception\_only} format (correct executions raise no exceptions, so the trace content is the same regardless of the solution's internal logic), the dataset contains duplicate rows.
Train--test input overlap is zero (split by problem ID), so no information leakage occurs.
The high duplication in \texttt{exception\_only} does not affect our experimental conclusions: after deduplication the training set still contains 2,858 unique samples and the test set 607, providing sufficient coverage for the 591-problem benchmark.

\paragraph{Problem-level partitioning and sensitivity analysis.}
Data is partitioned at the problem level: 472 training problems and 119 test problems, with zero crossover.
Duplicates arise from multiple candidate solutions per problem (up to 10 solutions each), not from cross-problem overlap.
To verify that deduplication does not alter any finding, we ran a sensitivity analysis across all 19 experimental conditions (7 trace formats $\times$ 4 models, minus conditions not run): deduplication produces a negligible ($<$0.1pp) accuracy delta in every case.
This shows that duplicate samples neither inflate nor deflate accuracy, because duplicates share the same ground-truth label and the model's prediction is deterministic at inference time.
Duplicates arise because the \texttt{exception\_only} format collapses passing solutions (which share identical ``no exception'' output) into identical rows; the redundancy is a property of the format's compactness for pass-class samples.
The \texttt{exception\_only} test set contains 48.99\% such duplicates; all confidence intervals treat samples as independent Bernoulli trials.

\paragraph{Why SFT over regex?}

SFT \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%) exceeds the best regex (B5, 99.33\%) by 0.50pp on caught-exception boundary cases (McNemar $p{=}.014$), provides calibrated probabilities (ECE\,=\,0.0027; \S\ref{sec:calibration}), and retains 97.65\% under marker removal vs.\ B5's 28.49\% (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).
Bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) with near-majority \texttt{no\_trace} performance shows the learned patterns are language-level, not dataset-specific.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four code-specialized models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while compact exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness show SFT acquires genuine diagnostic patterns.
An empirical two-tier signal hierarchy and controlled masking ablation (gradient dilution accounts for ${\leq}$4\% of the gap; content quality at inference explains the majority, though forward-pass information flow is a residual confound) suggest that diagnostic density, not information quantity, is the binding constraint.
For practitioners building trace-based SFT pipelines, the recommendation is direct: prioritize exception events; when unavailable, tail-truncated traces at ${\geq}$512 tokens provide a viable fallback at 93--97\% accuracy.
Whether these patterns extend to larger (30B+) or general-purpose models remains open.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four code-specialized models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while compact exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness show SFT acquires genuine diagnostic patterns.
An empirical two-tier signal hierarchy and controlled masking ablation (gradient dilution accounts for ${\leq}$4\% of the gap; content quality at inference explains the majority, though forward-pass information flow is a residual confound) suggest that diagnostic density, not information quantity, is the binding constraint.
For practitioners building trace-based SFT pipelines: prioritize exception events; when unavailable, tail-truncated traces at ${\geq}$512 tokens provide a viable fallback at 93--97\% accuracy, though extension to larger (30B+) or general-purpose models remains open.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four code-specialized models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while compact exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness show SFT acquires genuine diagnostic patterns.
An empirical two-tier signal hierarchy and controlled masking ablation (gradient dilution accounts for ${\leq}$4\% of the gap; content quality at inference explains the majority, though forward-pass information flow is a residual confound) suggest that diagnostic density, not information quantity, is the binding constraint.
For practitioners building trace-based SFT pipelines: prioritize exception events; when unavailable, tail-truncated traces (${\geq}$512 tokens) provide a viable fallback at 93--97\% accuracy; generalization beyond 13B or code-specialized models remains open.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four code-specialized models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces achieve only 77--82\% while compact exception events reach ${\geq}$99.33\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness show SFT acquires genuine diagnostic patterns.
An empirical two-tier signal hierarchy and controlled masking ablation (gradient dilution accounts for ${\leq}$4\% of the gap; content quality at inference explains the majority, though forward-pass information flow is a residual confound) suggest that diagnostic density, not information quantity, is the binding constraint.
For practitioners building trace-based SFT pipelines: prioritize exception events; when unavailable, tail-truncated traces (${\geq}$512 tokens) provide a viable fallback at 93--97\% accuracy; generalization beyond 13B or code-specialized models remains open.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four code-specialized models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces achieve only 77--82\% while compact exception events reach ${\geq}$99.33\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness show SFT acquires genuine diagnostic patterns.
An empirical two-tier signal hierarchy and controlled masking ablation (gradient dilution accounts for ${\leq}$4\% of the gap; content quality at inference explains the majority, though forward-pass information flow is a residual confound) suggest that diagnostic density, not information quantity, is the binding constraint.
For practitioners building trace-based SFT pipelines: prioritize exception events; when unavailable, tail-truncated traces (${\geq}$512 tokens) provide a viable fallback at 93--97\% accuracy; generalization beyond 13B or code-specialized models remains open.
